about:
Michigan Freeze Pack operates from Hart, Michigan, in the heart of the state's prime vegetable-growing region. The company was established in 1988 as a grower-owned cooperative and remains a multi-generational family enterprise. Its farmer-owners built the facility to process vegetables grown on their own lands, creating a direct link between field and freezer.

The 100,000-square-foot plant specializes in individually quick frozen (IQF) vegetables for the ingredient market. Core products include asparagus, butternut squash, cabbage, carrots, celery, green zucchini, potatoes, and yellow zucchini. The operation offers custom processing, blending, packing, and cold storage, and can also contract-grow specific varieties for customers who meet volume thresholds. Clients may supply their own raw material for toll processing.

Michigan Freeze Pack serves food ingredient manufacturers and distributors who require consistent, specification-driven frozen vegetables. Its customer base includes companies that incorporate IQF vegetables into prepared meals, soups, sauces, and retail frozen blends. The USDA-inspected facility supports both conventional and organic production lines.

The grower-owned structure is central to the company's value proposition: it enables a "Grown and Processed in the USA" claim, ensures traceability from seed to package, and aligns with sustainable farming practices. The cooperative model also allows rapid response to customer specifications while maintaining the environmental stewardship the founding families prioritize.
